text:
maya: heads up — we're seeing ~12% median token latency regression on /v1/generate since the 12:30 UTC deploy. Token-level breakdown points to a stall in the KV lookup stage. SM occupancy dropped to ~42% (normally ~63%). VRAM per-worker up ~1.4GB. Any theories?

sam: can you drop the per-route KPIs dash link and the model+rev? will check infra noise too.

maya: model=falcon-7b-quant-v2, pinned rev=a, no gradual rollout. dash: https://dash.redwood/internal/perf/route/generate?since=20m .

liam: re: profiling — kicked off perfbot job against the affected hosts (r-infer-24..27) to capture kernel timelines, memcpy, and KV latency.

perfbot: profiling job #194 queued for hosts [r-infer-24,r-infer-25,r-infer-26,r-infer-27]. collecting NVML, CUPTI kernel spans, and PMU samples. ETA ~4m.

ana: (typo corrected) ana: quick check — can you paste KV cache hit ratio and p95 kv_lookup? if prefetch/backoff changed we might be spamming memcpy.

perfbot: job #194 finished. summary: https://perf.redwood/jobs/194/summary 
- flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/jobs/194/flame.svg 
- note: kernel-selector fell back to generic_matmul for ~18% of batches where seq_len > 512. memcpy spikes line up with KV prefetch retries. average SM occupancy=44%, power +8W, GPU temp +3C from baseline.

sam: interesting — kernel-selector fallback aligned with a TensorRT plugin tweak in rev=a? @liam any kernel selector changes recently?

liam: I reverted the speculative kernel-selector heuristic on canary ~3h ago, but prod still had it. unrelated? Also batching heuristic (beta) bumped pad_coalesce_window 8->12 yesterday. that can group long sequences differently.

maya: that could explain more seq>512 batches being coalesced causing selector to choose fallback optimized for large blocks (which we don't have kernels for). KV p95 jumped from 2.1ms -> 9.6ms in the same window.

ana: quick metric query I ran: 
```
SELECT route, percentile(token_latency_ms, [50,95,99]) as p FROM metrics.tokens WHERE route='/v1/generate' AND ts > now() - 30m GROUP BY route
```
shows a step at 12:31 UTC. KV hit ratio stayed ~96% but prefetch retry count doubled.

sam: I'll add a temporary token-stage waterfall widget (queue -> kernel_enqueue -> kv_lookup -> memcpy -> kernel_exec -> postproc) and surface per-MIG slice SM occupancy (NVML per slice). if MIG metrics missing we need nvml exporter tweak.

liam: FYI logs on r-infer-25 show repeated MIG slice reassignments around the spike; looks like a MIG pause triggered fallback to non-MIG path for some workloads. that would explain occupancy drop and VRAM increase.

maya: proposed immediate actions: 1) revert pad_coalesce_window to 8, 2) put kernel-selector into strict-mode to avoid generic fallback for common seq lengths, 3) increase KV prefetch backoff and reduce retry aggression. thumbs?

ana: +1 revert batching. also we should add alert rule: if SM occupancy delta > 10% across identical worker pool in 5m then page oncall.

sam: filing INF-4213 with the canary & prod diffs, linking flamegraph and dash. https://issues.redwood/INF-4213 (assigned to liam/sam/maya).

liam: starting canary patch to revert batching now. will monitor the token-waterfall and SM occupancy.

maya: thanks — I'll watch the dashboard and post updated token-level breakdown in 15m.

deploy-bot: canary deploy 1768499800 -> 1768499900 completed for r-infer-canary (note: includes batching beta). :eyes:

perfbot: reminder: I captured COP kernels and NVTX spans in job #194 — useful to compare kernel durations pre/post revert.

sam: final note — long-term: add per-route steady-state SM occupancy baselines and a dashboard for MIG slice thermal/power correlated with kernel type. that will make root-cause faster.

maya: agreed. thanks everyone — will update once canary results are in.
